# Multi-model transcribe

Local transcription with several faster-whisper models, one after another, plus an optional merge that majority-votes the outputs, and a short written summary. No API key, no Hugging Face token. The audio never leaves the machine it runs on; the assistant reads the transcript text (not the audio) to write the summary.

## Models (pass as `--models a,b,c`)

- base: fastest (~30x realtime), rough — quick drafts, sanity checks
- small: fast (~13x), fair — good cheap second opinion
- distil-large-v3: medium (~7x), very good, English — best speed/quality default
- distil-large-v3.5: medium (~8x), very good+, English (distil-whisper/distil-large-v3.5-ct2)
- large-v3-turbo: slower (~3x est.), excellent, multilingual (deepdml/faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo-ct2)
- medium: slowest (~2x est.), good, multilingual, older

Speeds measured on an 8-core CPU with int8 (est. = not measured), excluding a 3-16 s model load; a CUDA GPU is 10x+ faster. First use of each model downloads it once (75 MB for base up to ~1.6 GB for large-v3-turbo). Suggested default: `distil-large-v3,small` (add `base` for a 3-way vote).

## Steps

1. Save the transcription script to a working folder as `mmt.py` (write it once; reuse it). The script is a self-contained Python/faster-whisper program: it takes audio/video files or folders (searched recursively), transcribes each file with each requested model one model at a time, writes per-model outputs, and optionally merges. It needs Python >=3.9 and faster-whisper>=1.1; it sets HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN and HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY so no token is ever sent.
2. Check `ffmpeg` is on PATH (optional but preferred; the script falls back to its built-in decoder). Check `uv` (preferred) or install with `pip install faster-whisper`.
3. Run, on whichever machine holds the audio: `uv run mmt.py <file-or-folder> --models distil-large-v3,small --formats txt,srt,json [--merge]`. Without uv: `pip install faster-whisper && python mmt.py ...`. GPU is auto-detected (float16); CPU uses int8. Override with `--device cpu|cuda --compute-type ...`. `--language en` skips detection. `--out DIR` changes the output root. `--force` redoes existing outputs. For more than ~2 minutes of audio, start it in the background and wait for the completion notice instead of polling.
4. Outputs: `<out>/<file stem>/transcript.<model>.txt|srt|json`; with `--merge`, also `transcript.merged.txt|srt|json`. Default `<out>` is `transcripts/` next to the input. Existing outputs are skipped, including merged files once all requested merged formats exist; safe to re-run after an interruption. `--force` redoes both. Supported inputs include mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg, opus, wma, webm, mp4, mkv, mov, m4b, aiff/aif. Non-distil files are converted to 16 kHz mono wav with ffmpeg when available. The script also supports `--pivot NAME`, `--threads`, `--beam`, `--no-vad`, and `--list-models`.
5. Merge: every model is aligned word-by-word to the best-ranked model (the pivot, or `--pivot NAME`), each word is majority-voted, and a word only one model heard is shown as `[?word]`. `transcript.merged.json` holds per-word votes, alternatives where models disagreed, and an agreement %. Needs 2+ models; 3+ gives a real vote.
6. Summary: for each file, read `transcript.merged.txt` from its output folder (or, with no merge, the best-ranked model's transcript, using the model order above) and write `summary.md` in that same folder: a short overview paragraph, then a few key-point bullets. Skip a file whose `summary.md` already exists unless the user asked to redo (or the run used `--force`). This step is done by the assistant from the transcript text; the audio itself is never sent anywhere.
7. Report back: files, models, wall time per model, output folder, merge agreement %, a 2-3 line sample, and the summary (overview + key points from each `summary.md`). Do not paste whole transcripts into chat.

## Copy after transcription (off by default)

Copying is **off** unless the user turns it on and chooses a destination. Modes:

- **off** (default): keep outputs only in the local output folder described above.
- **finals only**: copy the final outputs for each input file — `transcript.merged.{txt,srt,json}` for the requested formats when `--merge` was run (if no merge was run, the best-ranked model's `transcript.<model>.{txt,srt,json}` for the requested formats) — plus `summary.md` when it was written.
- **all transcripts**: copy everything in *finals only*, plus every per-model output `transcript.<model>.{txt,srt,json}` for the requested formats.

Rules for either copy mode:

- The destination is the user's own choice: a folder path on a machine they control, or a folder in a connected cloud storage service they choose. Never assume or hard-code a destination.
- Before the first copy, ask the user to confirm the exact destination (service/folder and path), then verify it with a small test file/copy and read the result back before copying any transcript.
- Copy, never move: never delete local transcripts or any other local output, even after a successful copy.
- If a copy fails or the destination is unreachable, report the failure, keep all local outputs, and do not silently substitute a different destination.
- Enabling copy applies to new runs going forward; do not backfill earlier transcripts unless the user explicitly asks.

---

description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: pick where audio lives, default models,
  output formats, and the off-by-default copy option, then save them to memory.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line: "I transcribe your audio/video locally with one or more Whisper models and can merge them into a majority-vote transcript. No keys; your audio never leaves the machine it runs on. I read the transcript text to write you a short summary."

Ask one at a time, skipping any already in memory:

1. **Where does the audio live?** Your registered computer (I run there, it needs `uv` or Python + `pip install faster-whisper`, ffmpeg recommended), or my own computer (drop files in chat and I copy them over). If the runner is your registered computer, each command I run there asks you to approve it in the app (local-tool approval), so expect a few approval prompts on the first job.
2. **Default models?** Show: base (fastest, rough), small (fast, fair), distil-large-v3 (~7x realtime on CPU, very good, English — recommended), distil-large-v3.5 (similar speed, slightly better, English), large-v3-turbo (slower, best, multilingual), medium (slowest, good, multilingual). Suggest `distil-large-v3,small` (add `base` for a 3-way vote). Mention first use downloads each model once.
3. **Outputs?** Any of txt, srt, json, merged (merged needs 2+ models).
4. **Copy after transcription?** Off by default. If they want copies, ask: finals only (merged/final transcript files plus `summary.md`) or all transcripts (finals plus every per-model output and `summary.md`), and where to — a folder path or a cloud folder they choose. Confirm the exact destination with them and verify it with a small test before the first real copy. Never delete local transcripts, and never backfill old transcripts unless they ask.

Then write each answer to memory as a convention (e.g. "Audio runner: <machine>", "Default models: ...", "Formats: ...", "Copy after transcription: off" or "...: finals only / all transcripts -> <user-chosen destination>"), save the script from the Multi-model transcribe skill on the runner machine, and say: "Ready. Drop a file or folder (or give a path)." Don't transcribe anything until they do.
